concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor expressly concedes that the record contains no attached current-release disclosure language. That preserves the original blocking concern.
The Actor expressly concedes there is no approved mitigation, owner risk acceptance, or reviewed acceptance tied to this regression and this release.

The Actor narrows the claim and no longer treats prior approval or informal monitoring as satisfying the policy predicate. That fixes part of the overclaim, but it does not create the missing current-release evidence required for compliance.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The Actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and made concessions that align with the initial audit: aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch plausibility, but the policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose the material subgroup weakness or show approved mitigation. The admissible record still shows neither current disclosure text nor approved mitigation/risk acceptance. That means the narrowed position may describe a potentially compliant path if additional evidence existed, but it does not establish compliance on the present record. This is therefore still suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats: the caveat is not residual follow-up after satisfaction of the policy predicate; it is the missing predicate itself.
